newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt sale to drag on.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt sale to drag on.

text.p: The six-year long efforts by the Austrian government to sell its stake in Creditanstalt on Monday looked set to drag on after the only clear bidder said its offer had been rejected by Finance Minister Viktor Klima.

EA Generali, who heads the Austro-Italian-German group bidding for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt-Bankverein, said its offer fell short as it did not cover taking over the entire stake.
"The consortium regrets that it was not able to fully meet the expectations of the Finance Ministry," EA Generali said in a press statement.
"It can therefore be expected, that a new round of bidding will follow."

The consortium, which also includes Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commerciale Italiana, remains interested in Austria's flagship bank and cited "a particular wish to include savings bank Die Erste in mutual considerations over the privatisation of CA."

Finance Minister Klima over the past two weeks has repeatedly hinted the group's bid, submitted on September 6 just hours before a government deadline expired, failed to meet his demands for an all-cash offer for the government's entire 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt.

EA-Generali reportedly offered cash for about half the government's 19.9 million Creditanstalt shares and proposed to sell the rest in a secondary offering, possibly financed via a convertible bond issue.

The consortium was thrown into disarray just hours before Klima's deadline expired when Die Erste, Austria's biggest savings bank, left the group after hectic negotiations with its partners failed to produce agreement on a joint bid.
Die Erste has left its options open in what has become Austria's longest-running privatisation drama, saying it was waiting for Klima's final word and would then re-evaluate its position.
Klima, desperate to use the proceeds from the sale to fill the government's bare coffers, is now expected to reopen the privatisation process to other potential bidders.

A host of international candidates, among them Allianz Holding of Germany and CS Holding of Switzerland, over the past few years have lost interest in Creditanstalt after what they felt was a bias against foreign ownership in Austria.
